Resolves #21425

A tile entry in `example-captures.json` may now give its component a capture size (`{path, width, height}`). The recipe applies that size to the stage component before measuring, just as it already hides a field's other states. 21 field tiles take 220 px, and IBAN and the copy-to-clipboard trigger take 224 px. Their regions shrink from 348–388 px to 268–272 px, so their 14 px text shows at 9.1 px instead of 6–7 px on a 175 px tile. The checkbox keeps its natural size: at 220 px its box label wraps, which the cold read caught. One headless run recaptured all 45 tiles. The bytes are on neomjs/pages#118 under the same names, and the checkbox tile's natural-size bytes are on neomjs/pages#121, so no catalog record changes.

Evidence: L3 (one recipe run with its report, the recipe's unit spec, frames of Forms & Fields with the new bytes routed in, one cold read) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-5). Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket

- AC-1 was amended on the ticket after the first runs. A width or height bound does not narrow the lists, File upload, Range, Fieldset, Date selector, Form layout, Nested templates or Sitemap below their own content, and cropping them would break AC-2. Each is captured at its smallest region, listed above.
- The entry also takes a `height`, for components whose 4:3 region their height decides (Text area, Date selector, Form layout, Nested templates, Monaco editor, Sitemap).
- The checkbox keeps its natural size, because at 220 px its box label wraps. The cold read found it.

The after frames predate `07b6589f77`, so their checkbox tile still shows the wrapped label. Larger tiles (#21140 design 6) remain the bigger lever and are raised there.

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-11-19T03:46:47Z

## AC-5: the cold read

One fresh reader (a front-end engineer evaluating component libraries) was given only the four frames, labelled A and B, and not told which was new. They graded the new tiles 7/10 and today's 3/10 at 1440 × 900 (4/10 at 390 × 844), and would ship the new ones. Their five-second read of the new frame: *"I can actually read what's in most of them"*; of today's: *"a wall of tiny grey input boxes."*

What I did with each point:

- **Checkbox: "the label wraps awkwardly, leaving 'notes' alone on a second line."** My 220 px width caused it. The box label stays on one line only from 272 px, wider than the field's own 265 px content box, so the entry goes back to its natural size. Recaptured headless at a 313 px region, the tile is byte-identical to the one before neomjs/pages#118. The manifest change and a one-file pages PR follow on this PR's next head.
- **Email, IBAN and Invite link (copy-to-clipboard) clip their values** inside their own inputs: "jane.doe@example.", "DE89 3704 0044 0532", "https://neomj". No crop cuts a component (AC-2 holds). This is what AC-1's 272 px bound costs a field whose value is longer than its input. Kept as is: whole values at 9 px need wider tiles, which is the density lever on #21140 (design 6).
- **Form layout and Date selector are unreadable in both versions.** They don't narrow below their content (AC-1's named list), so the same lever applies.
- **The dim floating labels and File upload's brown button** come from the neo dark theme's drawing, not the crops. The File upload button already has a defect-note from 19 Nov.
- The shell points (the count line, the footnote, the build control) were relayed to the shell's owners on 19 Nov.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5.5 · Claude Code
